text.p: U.S. stocks were seen opening lower on Wednesday after the February Consumer Price Index rose 0.3 percent, analysts said.
The core rate, excluding food and energy components, rose 0.2 percent.
Economists in a Reuters survey had forecast a rise, on average, of 0.2 percent in the overall CPI and a 0.2 percent rise in the core rate.
Jim Solloway, director of research at Argus Research said: "The numbers were a bit worse than consensus, so the gains that we had at the beginning of trading in the bond market have been erased."
"That's going to perhaps reduce the optimism regarding the stock market's opening this morning...(The stock market will open) either a little off or not as strongly as had been initially expected."

Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp, said: "If you're going to put a good or bad label, it's bad. But neither label is appropriate. It's not a jolt to the market. On balance, the index came in above expectations, but not so much so that it will scare the markets."
